text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Russian proposal for a meeting among the representatives of the five permanent members of the U.N. Security Council on the Cyprus problem has been accepted.
- Council of Ministers waives many of the restrictive rules regarding foreign investments in Cyprus. Policies on investments by Cypriots abroad are redefined.
- Cyprus President Glafcos Clerides rejects British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind's fears of conflict over Cyprus. President says Turkey unlikely to risk war over Cyprus.

- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, in a statement before the House International Relations Committee in Washington, stressed America's determination to play a greater role in the efforts to find a Cyprus solution.
- Political parties reject Rifkind's remarks that both sides lack the political will to find a solution to the Cyprus problem.
- Important changes in operation and development of public companies are likely to happen following a bill presented by the government to the parliament for the Cyprus Stock Exchange.
